problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,t\in [0,\pi )$ find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\cdot ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t) & =0 \\ -8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in [0,\pi )$, the only solutions are $t=0$ and $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡0\,,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩=⟨0\,,\,3⟩, \\ r(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}⟩=⟨1\,,\,0⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the points $(0,3)$ and $(1,0).$
